newsitem.title: UK: UK should stay out of EMU if criteria fudged - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: UK should stay out of EMU if criteria fudged - Clarke.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Sunday Britain should stay out of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) if the convergence criteria were to be relaxed.
"We should stay out (of EMU) if they fudged the convergence criteria," said Clarke, speaking on British television's 'On the Record' programme.

"At this stage we have to decide to keep ourselves involved. We should be a leading member of the European Union," said Clarke. "We should be realising we are competing very well against the Germans and French and should have as much influence as them."
Clarke said he was flatly against handing over control of taxation and public spending to Europe.

"Until we know which countries are joining, the state of their economies and what basis they are going to run a single monetary policy, it is not in the national interest to make a decision," said Clarke.
